criteria.description: Resource and booking creation/listing persist across processes, repeat initialization preserves data, database paths are independent, IDs support case-sensitive spaces/Unicode, capacity is immutable, and cancelled IDs stay reserved.

Strict UTC timestamps and positive integer inputs are validated; active quantities obey capacity at every instant under half-open intervals, including adjacent endpoints and multiple overlaps; rejected operations preserve records.

Cancellation is idempotent and releases capacity; active booking rescheduling excludes the old interval and atomically changes start/end/quantity, preserving old values on rejection; missing/cancelled transitions reject as specified; concurrent CLI mutations cannot overbook.
Read-only availability returns capacity minus peak active occupancy across the entire query, not the sum of intersecting bookings, with correct clipping, endpoints, and cancelled-booking exclusion.

JSON imports validate the exact required arrays/fields/types, reject duplicate keys and booleans as integers, resolve existing and batch resources, and validate whole-batch capacity. Success commits all items; malformed or rejected batches commit none. Dry run uses equivalent validation without persisting records.

Explicit-interval reports include every resource and correct capacity, peak active quantity, and clipped booked unit-seconds, excluding cancelled bookings and outside time without dependence on the current clock.

The required python3 -m booking_ledger entry point provides discoverable help, human and JSON outputs for specified operations, deterministic ID ordering, resource/status booking filters, useful errors/nonzero rejection without expected-input tracebacks, path-with-spaces support, and read-only rejection of uninitialized databases.

The delivered project uses only Python standard library and SQLite, works end to end, has coherent maintainable implementation and runnable README setup/workflow examples, and meaningful tests runnable through python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v covering actual CLI/persistence, intervals, rollback, imports, dry run, and reports.

The complete delivered CLI, implementation, tests, and README agree with the fixed prompt. Cross-feature UTC/half-open/cancellation/capacity/validation rules stay consistent, all requested outcomes are implemented rather than replaced with a smaller demo, and unfinished requirements are reported accurately.

existing_tests: python3 -c 'import sys, sqlite3, unittest; assert sys.version_info >= (3, 12); assert sqlite3.connect(":memory:").execute("select 1").fetchone() == (1,)'
evaluator_guidance: Derive all checks from the candidate prompt, using each candidate's documented command names, flags, JSON layout, and supported setup. The only fixed entry points are python3 -m booking_ledger and python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v. The existing_tests command is an environment smoke check, not application coverage; run candidate tests and additional adaptive CLI journeys. Use isolated temporary database/file paths, including spaces, and inspect persisted records after rejected operations. Cover tied endpoints, staggered overlaps whose pairwise checks miss aggregate capacity, disjoint bookings where summing overlaps understates availability, successful self-excluding reschedule, failed reschedule rollback, cancellation effects across availability/report/import, late import conflicts, dry-run parity, malformed JSON/types, concurrent writers, and clipped unit-seconds. Requirements, not one preferred architecture or output schema, determine correctness. For requirement-retention, execute a cross-feature journey and compare code/tests/README with exact prompt requirements; identify omissions, contradictions, and accurately disclosed incompleteness separately. Use source inspection for maintainability and documentation consistency without treating it as runtime proof. Expected evaluator wiring errors remain HARNESS_ERROR/unassessed. Do not use agent arm labels, journal/reset counts, runtime length, or launcher-specific workflow compliance to score product quality; judge blind. Reset qualification is a separate operator analysis. No solution or prewritten hidden checks are supplied.
